customMachines.name: Custom machines — two stacks, a queue

whatIsThis.heading: What is this?
whatIsThis.body1: AutomataLab is an interactive workshop for
whatIsThis.subject: Formal Languages and Automata Theory
whatIsThis.body2: : finite automata, pushdown automata, Turing machines and generative grammars can be defined, simulated and transformed. Everything works offline, worksheets are saved to the browser automatically.

machines.heading: Machines — a single model
machines.body1: Every machine is built with the same
machines.body2: key: a finite control plus any number of storages.
machines.emphasis: Its kind is decided by the configuration
machines.body3: — no storage means a finite automaton, one stack means a pushdown automaton, one tape (holding the input) means a Turing machine, another combination means a general machine. The interface recognizes it and names it accordingly.
machines.example:
Machine:               # finite automaton: no storage
  name: M1
  charset: a, b
  states: S, A, F
  init: S
  accept: F
  transitions:
    - S . S      # "." = every letter of the alphabet
    - S a A
    - A b F      # ε-transition: S ε A (type eps)

expressions.heading: Expressions
expressions.body1: In a new cell you can reference machines and perform operations in the form
expressions.body2: . If an operation's precondition is missing (e.g. ε-freedom for determinization), the app explains why and inserts the fix chain with one click.

ops.completeReachable: completion with a trap state / removing unreachable states
ops.regex: a regular expression as a value — toFsm() turns it into an automaton
ops.conversions: conversions between automaton ↔ grammar, grammar → pushdown automaton
ops.namedOps: operations between named automata: concatenation, union, closure — letter literals only inside regex(…)

expressions.optionalName: The name is optional: without one the result is still shown, it just can't be referenced from other cells — like an unnamed expression in Desmos.

storages.heading: Storages: stack, queue, tape
storages.example:
Machine:               # pushdown automaton: one stack
  name: AnBn
  charset: a, b
  states: q0, q1, q2
  init: q0
  accept: q2           # or acceptMode: emptyStorages
  storages:
    stack: stack       # the stack starts with Z by default; otherwise:
  transitions:         #   stack: { type: stack, init: X }
    - q0 a Z/AZ q0     # reading a: push AZ instead of Z
    - q0 b A/ε q1      # ε = push nothing
    - q1 ε Z/Z q2      # ε-step (type eps)

Machine:               # Turing machine: one tape, holding the input
  name: T
  charset: a, b
  states: s, ok
  init: s
  accept: ok
  input: tape          # the input is placed on this storage
  storages:
    tape: tape
  transitions:
    - s a/b > s        # read a, write b, move right
    - s _/& = ok       # _ = blank symbol, & = write the same symbol back
storages.body2: — a stack/queue takes one element (POP/PUSH), a tape takes two (read/write move). Any number of storages can be combined: two stacks already build a Turing-power machine (e.g. aⁿbⁿcⁿ, which is impossible with a pushdown automaton), a queue gives a queue automaton. The automaton operations (det, min…) only apply to storage-free machines — the app explains why.

grammar.heading: Grammar
grammar.example:
Grammar:
  name: G
  charset: a, b
  variables: S
  init: S
  rules:
    - S -> aSb | ε   # type eps for ε; \eps = the letters
grammar.body: The grammar view automatically determines the class according to the Chomsky hierarchy, and for every level shows which rule violates it and why.

fsm.completeHint: Every (state, symbol) pair has a transition.

grammar.title: Grammar
grammar.epsilonFreeHint: ε occurs at most as S → ε, and S never appears on a right-hand side.
grammar.type3Holds: Every rule has the form A → uB or A → u (u a terminal string).
grammar.type2Holds: Every rule's left-hand side is a single nonterminal.
grammar.type1Holds: No rule shortens the string (except the allowed S → ε).
grammar.noDerivableWords: No derivable word found up to length 8.
grammar.moreWordsPossible: …the language may be larger than this (the enumeration covers length 8).
